subject.one_line: An Ethereum protocol for borrowing a dollar-targeted token against staked IMD.

summary.text: imdUSD is a token on Ethereum designed to be worth one US dollar.
The project names miyagod.eth as its founder, and a wallet that needs two of its three signers governs the borrowing settings.
If you hold staked IMD, you can put it up as collateral through the project’s website and borrow imdUSD against it.
Borrowers pay Ethereum transaction fees and annual interest, which was about 4.4% when last checked.
Holders can exchange imdUSD for staked IMD worth up to a dollar per token before a redemption fee of 0.5% to 5%.
The system uses signed price answers from IdentityMD agent panels, and stale or disagreeing prices can stop borrowing and redemption.
The documentation gives lower minimums for the number of agents and agreements than the deployed price feeds use.
About 60,000 imdUSD existed when last checked.

lines.text: imdUSD is a token designed to be worth one US dollar.
lines.quote: stablecoin meant to be worth one US dollar

lines.text: The protocol runs on Ethereum mainnet.
The protocol lets people borrow imdUSD against staked IMD.
lines.quote: locking staked IMD in a vault

lines.text: The vault stakes plain IMD for borrowers who deposit it.
Holders can redeem imdUSD for staked IMD.
lines.quote: Anyone can burn imdUSD and receive sIMD

lines.text: Borrowers use a connected wallet to act in the web terminal.
lines.quote: You connect a browser wallet to act

lines.text: Keepers relay prices and liquidate unsafe loans.
lines.quote: relays price updates, marks unsafe positions or liquidates them.

lines.text: Borrowers need ETH for transaction fees.
lines.quote: and a little ETH for gas.

lines.text: Borrowers pay annual interest on their loan principal.
lines.quote: Annual stability fee on principal, in basis points.

lines.text: Redemption fees range from 0.5% to 5%.
The vault holds every borrowing position.
Only the vault can mint or burn imdUSD.
lines.quote: only contract that mints or burns imdUSD

lines.text: The imdUSD token has no owner.
The imdUSD token has no pause switch.
The imdUSD token has no upgrade path.
A loan is unsafe when its collateral ratio falls below the required minimum.
The minimum collateral ratio rises as the network health measure falls.
lines.quote: the minimum collateral ratio, which rises as network health falls.

lines.text: An unsafe loan must be marked before it can be liquidated.
Liquidators are paid from the liquidation bonus.
lines.quote: keepers are paid from the liquidation bonus.

lines.text: Interest accrues without compounding.
The annual borrowing rate at launch was 4.44%.
The Treasury receives paid interest.
lines.quote: Receives the protocol's bonus share and paid fees.

lines.text: Redemption pays at most one dollar of staked IMD per token before fees.
lines.quote: worth $1, or the backing per imdUSD if that is lower

lines.text: The Treasury is the first source of staked IMD for redemptions.
lines.quote: Redemption is paid from the Treasury's sIMD first.

lines.text: Larger redemptions can raise the redemption fee.
lines.quote: A larger burn raises the fee

lines.text: imdUSD trades against USDC in a Uniswap v4 pool.
lines.quote: against USDC in one Uniswap v4 pool.

lines.text: A swap near the dollar target pays a 0.01% pool fee.
Swaps that push the price far enough away from one dollar pay a surcharge.
Swap surcharges go to the Treasury.
lines.quote: The surcharge goes to the Treasury

lines.text: An oracle service signs collateral price answers from IdentityMD agent panels.
lines.quote: the oracle service signs the answer.

lines.text: The documentation gives 25 agents as the minimum panel size.
lines.quote: a panel of at least 25 agents

lines.text: The documentation gives 15 agreeing agents as the feed threshold.
The dollar calculation uses Chainlink’s ETH price.
lines.quote: The ETH/USD price comes from Chainlink

lines.text: Stale or disagreeing prices can block borrowing and redemption.
Borrowers can still deposit and repay when prices are stale.
A liquidation can leave unpaid debt.
lines.quote: records the rest as bad debt.

lines.text: The protocol has no insurance fund for bad debt.
INFER is the protocol token.
People can stake INFER for sINFER.
The INFER page says the Treasury buys INFER with protocol revenue.
lines.quote: The Treasury buys INFER with the protocol's revenue

lines.text: The project counts staked INFER as circulating.
The project excludes Treasury-held imdUSD from circulating supply.
Wallet holders earn one point per imdUSD per day.
Liquidators earn three days of holding points per imdUSD of debt repaid.
lines.quote: 3 days of holding points for each imdUSD of debt it repays.

lines.text: Each rewards season lasts 91 days.
INFER BOX accepts imdUSD payments to run requests through IdentityMD.
lines.quote: pay in imdUSD on Ethereum mainnet from the website and the swarm runs the request.

lines.rerun: On Ethereum mainnet (chain ID 1), fetch eth_getTransactionByHash and eth_getTransactionReceipt for 0x0d457379d83f6a32a252b2cad3754a1e36fcf3d432fd441e7fb73a6408bd5d5d via https://mainnet.gateway.tenderly.co. Expect block 26166419, status 0x1, from 0x5167D014a056E43883e1BBEa5530c3c0dC993281, to 0x4e59b44847b379578588920ca78fbf26c0b4956c, and a receipt log from 0x0b69F8DA8D8cE521d74Ea69a7A3475B77302EF82. differs.why: The documentation and the successful creation transaction put the same deployment in different Ethereum blocks.
The documented minimum panel size and the deployed feed constant differ for the same feeds.
The documented minimum agreement count and the deployed feed constant differ for the same feeds.
The contract establishes a minimum reported panel size, while the tracker says every price is answered by exactly that size of panel.
The audit brief describes a cold key before launch. The deployed settings point to a Safe, so the descriptions may refer to different versions.
A keeper or Treasury operator can carry out purchases even if the vault does not distribute revenue or buy tokens automatically.

open_questions: Which verified deployment and launch announcement will establish that the second version is live?
Do the IdentityMD price panels consistently report exactly 100 agents, or do accepted updates sometimes report larger panels?
Are there other publicly self-identified founders or operators, and do signed or on-chain records tie their profiles to the project?
Does the project’s X account publish the full main vault address in posts unavailable through the sources checked?
What was the market price of imdUSD for a specific trade size at the snapshot, after swap fees and price impact?
What role, if any, did the wallet address in the reported hackathon submission play in deploying the INFER token?
Who controls the two Safe signer wallets other than the deploying wallet?
notes: No earlier files or panel answers were supplied. The record covers the live Ethereum deployment identified by imdusd.com. IdentityMD Explorer lists a separate same-name launch with a different contract under launch 3293. No source checked ties that launch to this protocol. The core contract list follows the published address reference, the INFER launch listing and the supply endpoint. IMD, sIMD, IdentityMD Intake, Chainlink and the Uniswap pool manager are external dependencies. Off-domain channel ties describe the evidence found. The project links its X account, and the deployment wallet points to the founder ENS profile. The @yadfarms account association comes from public posts. No real-world identity is assigned. Proofs that use a snapshot generally refer to Ethereum block 26452404. The main vault address is published on the two protocol repositories, giving them a weak tie. ENS text records checked did not point to either X account. The contributor account is identified by its public GitHub handle. The checked links for GitHub and X establish attribution only to the named accounts. Some X posts were available through public mirrors. The source entries name those hosts. Update of 2026-11-20: all 143 lines from F1 were carried forward with their F1 ids; none were dropped. Time-varying proofs were re-read at Ethereum block 26458136 with the older reading kept in history. Supply rose from about 59,823 to about 60,022 imdUSD; the project supply endpoint now reports the newer figures, so its earlier statements were replaced by the newer ones from the same speaker. The site served a Cloudflare challenge to plain requests; pages loaded with a browser user agent. The logo is the apple-touch-icon from imdusd.com. No new blog posts appeared since October 21, 2026. A web search found no new outside coverage.
